ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an amide skeleton, the acyl carbon is connected to an R group, the carbonyl is C=O, and the nitrogen is HN and is connected to a -CH2-CH2-phenyl substituent. On the right side is POCl3, that is, P=O and bearing three Cl. The arrows show the electrons on nitrogen pushing toward the acyl carbon to form C=N, the electrons/oxygen of the carbonyl oxygen attacking the phosphorus center to form an O-P bond, while the electrons of one P-Cl bond move toward chlorine, causing one chlorine to leave. Reasoning: After electron rearrangement, the original carbonyl oxygen becomes an O-P(=O)(Cl)2 group connected to the carbon; nitrogen forms a double bond with the acyl carbon, and still retains H and the phenethyl substituent, so the nitrogen carries a positive charge and is written as [NH+]. The R group is retained as the wildcard [*] according to the problem statement, and the substituent on N is encoded as CCc1ccccc1. Therefore the SMILES of the product state is [*]/C(OP(Cl)(Cl)=O)=[NH+]/CCc1ccccc1.

method.method_draft: Inspect the image first: note the substrate skeleton R-C(=O)-NH-CH2CH2Ph and the reagent POCl3. Follow the arrows to relocate electrons: make the N-C pi bond, convert the carbonyl oxygen into an O-P(=O)(Cl)2 substituent, and remove the indicated chloride from phosphorus. Preserve the phenethyl substituent on nitrogen and the unspecified R group as [*]. Assign the nitrogen as [NH+] because it now has H, phenethyl, and a double bond to carbon. Encode the product as [*]/C(OP(Cl)(Cl)=O)=[NH+]/CCc1ccccc1.
